picks.why: Estate founded in 1997 at Agios Panteleimon on the Amyndeon plateau; its Reserve Vieilles Vignes comes from the Barba Yannis block, ungrafted bush vines of Xinomavro planted in 1919 that phylloxera never reached.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run: the wine is PDO Amyndeon, from one block of ungrafted bush vines planted in 1919 (an American drinks site's account of the estate and a merchant), with two years in French oak and a year in bottle for one vintage by its American importer. The label's words vary by source and by year (Xinomavro Reserve Vieilles Vignes Single Block Barba Yannis by two merchants, Barba Yannis Reserve Vieilles Vignes Xinomavro by a British critic's site, Ecosystem in earlier years), so the pick holds the block's name alone: give the label in full for the years taught. One account dates the first commercial wines to 2003: keep 1997 as the founding only with two sources. The Hedgehog single vineyard Xinomavro and its rosé go in others. Name no living founder.

picks.why: Estate begun in 2006 on the Amyndeon plateau and known above all for bottle fermented sparkling wine of Xinomavro; the Extra Cuvée de Réserve is its zero dosage blanc de noirs of ungrafted Xinomavro, left about five years on the lees by the house's own account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirmed in the thin run on the house's own sheet for the 2017 vintage, read through search: Xinomavro alone, ungrafted, zero dosage, a second fermentation in bottle and 54 to 84 months on the lees (five years by its terroir page), from vineyards in what the sheet calls a sub-region of the Amyndeo appellation; a Greek merchant places the vines at Agios Panteleimon, planted in 1970. IN DOUBT: whether the label carries PDO Amyndeon at all. The house's sheets title its Cuvée Spéciale a varietal sparkling wine and its rosé a varietal wine of Xinomavro and Limniona, and the appellation's sparkling wine is rosé by the Wines of Greece list of types, so a white sparkling wine may stand outside it: say what the label says and no more, and never call this wine the appellation's sparkling wine unless the label does. The house does bottle the appellation's own wine: a still red, Xinomavro Old Vines, sold as PDO Amyntaio by a British merchant, which goes in others first. 2006 is the founding by one merchant and the first vintage by another; the winery's village is Levea in one merchant's address and Filotas by a Greek travel site, so confirm it from the house. The Cuvée Spéciale (Xinomavro alone by one merchant, with a tenth of Assyrtiko by another), the Cuvée Rosé and the Cuvée Prestige go in others. The lane called the estate organic: confirm before saying so. Name no living founder.

picks.why: The growers' co-operative winery of Amyntaio town, at work since 1959 and since 2012 the winery of the Agricultural Cooperative of the Wider Amyntaio Area; its dry rosé of Xinomavro is the style Amyndeon alone holds as a PDO among the grape's appellations.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The lane's doubt is answered on the house's own pages (amyntaswines.gr, read through search): it lists a still dry rosé of Xinomavro alone under PDO Amyntaio, Rosé Xiros in its Amyntaio PDO range, beside a dry red and a Selected Vineyards red. It is not the Amyntas rosé (Xinomavro with a fifth of Syrah, PGI Florina) and not the sparkling Rosé Demi Sec and Rosé Sec (the Sec by the closed tank method), which go in others; a Greek wine writer calls the Demi Sec the house's emblem. The label's wording in Latin letters was not seen: give the name as the bottle carries it, and tell the read together agent if it cannot hold the pick's words. The house's names by source: Coop. Amynteo (Wines of Greece), Amyntas Wines (its own address and the regional tourism body), the winery of the Union of Agricultural Cooperatives of Amyntaio before 2012, by the house. One glossary dates the co-operative itself to 1945 and the winery to 1959; the house dates its first sparkling trials to 1971 and the appellation to 1972. Shares and volumes stay out.

picks.why: Family winery of Amyntaio where, by one account, winemaking began again in 2000 from an old family vineyard, after a family wine trade that went back before the Second World War; 7 Roots is its dry red of Xinomavro alone under the PDO.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line; a German wine glossary lists Hatzis among the appellation's known houses. Confirmed in the thin run: 7 Roots 2021 is sold by a Greek and an American merchant as a dry red of Xinomavro alone, PDO Amynteo, and a 2023 wine of the house is on sale in New York. Merchants print the house with its vintner's first name before the surname: confirm the name the label carries, and name no living person in prose. Confirm the founding (the restart of 2000 and the older family trade rest on one account: leave founded empty unless two agree), the village, the vineyard and the making of 7 Roots, and whether the house's older, oak aged Xinomavro has the stronger claim to be its flagship. Its blanc de noirs of Xinomavro, PGI Florina, goes in others.

picks.why: A winery on the outskirts of Agios Panteleimon, among the plateau's four lakes, written about in Greece and little seen abroad; its Xinomavro is a dry red of the grape alone under PDO Amyndeon, from vines of the village.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS and not in the region record's producers line. IN DOUBT, thin: the founding year, the owners and the house's own page were not found in the thin run, and every account found is Greek. What was confirmed: the regional tourism body lists the winery among those of Amyntaio open to visitors; a Greek wine magazine gives its Xinomavro 2019 as PDO Amyndeon, Xinomavro alone, from vineyards at Agios Panteleimon; a Greek Master of Wine reviewed the 2012, 2013 and 2014; a Greek writer's list of ten wines of Amyntaio names it. The author confirms the house, its founding and the wine's making from the house and a second source, or tells the merge agent, who may take the standby: Pavlou, an estate at Agios Panteleimon that worked with Xinomavro alone by an account of 2009, with a winery of 2006 and a red named Klima, which the same German glossary lists among the appellation's known houses but which no search of the thin run showed at work after about 2010. Name no living owner.
